small_guidance:
- Swap the GEMM-style accumulation orientation: use BLOCK_OC along the M-dim with BLOCK_HW along N-dim but compute w_vals as a [BLOCK_OC, 1] broadcast on a register-resident weight tile loaded once per (kh,kw,ic) — also try transposing so HW is the inner contiguous dim with BLOCK_HW=128/256 and BLOCK_OC=16/32 for better L1 reuse on the 16384-pixel maps.
- Add autotune configs with larger BLOCK_HW (512) and BLOCK_OC=16, plus num_stages=3-4 to overlap the 8*3*3=72 inner loads; current configs may not be hitting the best occupancy on small OC=64.
- Cache the weight tile in registers across the spatial-tile loop by reordering: load all (IC*KH*KW) weights for the OC tile once, then iterate spatial — since IC*KH*KW=72 and BLOCK_OC=32 fits easily in registers.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite with NHWC (channels-last) layout: permute input to (N, IH, IW, IC) so the GEMM-K dim (IC*KH*KW) is contiguous in memory, enabling vectorized loads along K. With IC=8 the K dim is tiny (72), so this lets each program do one tl.dot over [BLOCK_HW, 72] × [72, BLOCK_OC].
- Switch to an implicit-GEMM formulation: one program per (N, OH*OW tile, OC tile), accumulate via tl.dot with BLOCK_K=72 fully unrolled (KH, KW, IC all constexpr). Bias+ReLU+HardSwish fused in epilogue (already done). This replaces the triple Python-level loop with a single mma which is much faster on Ada.
- Consider packing weight as (IC*KH*KW, OC) at init in the module (still runs full conv at forward, just preshuffled W) so the inner tl.dot loads weights contiguously. This is a layout transform, not an algebraic shortcut.
